To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we have designed, synthesized and evaluated a series of novel non-nucleoside inhibitors of the cytosolic 2', 3'-cyclic nucleotide 3'-phosphodiesterase II (cND-II) and (2) we have demonstrated the synergistic effects of these compounds when used in combination of cytotoxic nucleos(t)ide analogues on different cancer cell lines.
we have developed a new series of non-nucleo(s)tide inhibitors of cN-II with potential usefulness to combat cancer drug resistance.
we have developed a series of novel cN-II inhibitors that are active in vitro and in vivo and are able to revert the resistance to cytotoxic agents.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design, synthesis and biological evaluation of a novel series of 2,6-diamino-9-(1H-imidazol-1-yl)-9H-purine derivatives as cN-II inhibitors, and their synergistic effects with cytotoxic nucleosides.
the development of new cN-II inhibitors and their potential use in the reversion of cancer drug resistance.
the identification and development of new non-nucleoside inhibitors of cN-II.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cN-II inhibition by the compounds herein described may be of therapeutic interest in cancer treatment.
the fragment-based approach has allowed the discovery of new cN-II inhibitors and the identification of a new chemical scaffold for the development of more active cN-II inhibitors.

the fragment-based design approach has been successful in identifying novel and potentially interesting inhibitors of cN-II, and the selected compounds may be considered as starting points for the development of new cN-II inhibitors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fragment-based approach has been successfully applied to generate new chemical scaffolds and to identify new chemical entities as potential inhibitors of the cN-II enzyme.

we have successfully used the Ilib-Diverse software to build a focused library of cN-II inhibitors and we have identified a new series of cN-II inhibitor with potential usefulness to revert resistance to nucleoside analogs.
the fragment-based approach combined to a molecular modeling program (Ilib-diverse) is a powerful strategy to generate new chemical entities with potential biological activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of a fragment-based approach with a computational program such as Ilib-diverse can be a valuable tool to design novel non-nucleoside inhibitors.

the use of fragment-based approaches in combination with molecular modelling and the Ilib-divers program, can provide a useful tool to design new chemical entities with potential therapeutic applications in cancer treatment.
fragment-based drug design can be a powerful tool in the development of non-nucleotidic compounds with potential therapeutic value.
